newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander retail banking jumps 30.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Santander retail banking jumps 30.6 pct.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Tuesday a 30.6 percent jump in retail banking operating income had helped boost 1996 results and pinpointed this area of its business as one of the foundations of future profitability.

"Reflecting a management commitment to maximising recurrent income, core business provided the backbone for 1996 results with Group retail banking business making up 78.8 percent of operating profit," the bank said in a statement.
It expected recurrent income business to provide a solid source of profits in the medium term.

"The Group attaches great importance to this recurring-income business and expects it to be one of the foundations of future profitability in the medium term," Santander's Chairman Emilio Botin said in a statement.
Within retail banking, Santander said it had increased its market share for mutual funds in Spain to 16.51 percent, becoming market leader.
"It was a landmark year, both abroad and also in Spain where the Group forged leadership in loans, deposits and mutual funds," Botin added.

Banco Santander said earlier on Tuesday 1996 net attributable profit rose to 85.60 billion pesetas from 75.39 billion pesetas. Net profit rose to 120.53 billion from 101.87 billion while pre-tax profit rose to 163.19 billion from 146.00 bilion pesetas.
